title: This “One-in-a-Million” Fish Has a Rare Genetic Condition That Turns It Yellow - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThis “One-in-a-Million” Fish Has a Rare Genetic Condition That Turns It YellowUS biologists just won the fish lotteryDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CST on November 18, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleBurbot (Lota lota), better known as cusk in northern New England, are usually green or brown, but the specimen just plucked out of Oswego Harbor on Lake Ontario is somehow a bright shade of yellow.It was discovered by biologists from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), who describe it as a “one-in-a-million” catch. The yellow hue is brought on by a rare genetic condition called xanthochromism, which suppresses red pigmentation to leave yellow at the fore. It can happen in birds and amphibians, as well as fish.Read more: “Scientists Catch a Rare Glimpse of a Fish With a See-Through Head”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
